svg.aria-label: Animated diagram in seven panels showing how a certificate, a NetSuite mapping and short-lived access tokens give an application machine-to-machine access to NetSuite.
svg.desc: Panel 1: generating a key pair gives a private key the application keeps and a certificate, with an expiry date chosen at that moment, that is uploaded to NetSuite. Panel 2: NetSuite ties the certificate to an integration record, a user and a role, and gives the mapping a Certificate ID. Panel 3: the application signs a request with the private key, NetSuite checks it against the certificate and returns an access token, which the application stores in Workers KV. Panel 4: the certificate lasts up to two years while each access token lasts 60 minutes and is replaced by signing a new request. Panel 5: a token request with an expired or revoked certificate, or an API request with an expired token, gets an error instead of a 200 response. Panel 6: several certificates on one integration record map different AI agents to different users and roles. Panel 7: NetSuite records the work under the user and role from the mapping.
svg.text: How the application proves who it is, what it is allowed to do, and for how long.

g.text: A certificate is a key pair with an expiry date
Made once. You choose how long it is valid at that moment; it cannot be extended later.
NetSuite ties the certificate to an integration, a user and a role
This is the mapping. One certificate belongs to exactly one combination.
what it is allowed to do
The application asks for an access token
It signs a short request with the private key. NetSuite checks it against the certificate it holds.
acts as the mapped user + role
Two clocks: a long-lived certificate, short-lived tokens
A token is cached, reused, then replaced. There is no refresh token: the app signs a new request.
expiry date, set when it was generated
before a token runs out, the app signs a new request (panel 3)
Workers KV holds the current token: one token request an hour, not one per API call
Expired or invalid: NetSuite answers with an error, not 200
Treat any answer that is not 200 as a failure. Which one it is tells you what to do next.
no access_token; reason: Login Audit Trail
What to do: generate a new certificate, upload it, store the new key and Certificate ID.
What to do: request a new token (panel 3), store it in KV, and retry the call once.
Several certificates on one integration: one role per job
Give each AI agent its own key and certificate, mapped to its own user and its own limited role.
AI agents · each holds its own private key
NetSuite · one integration record, three mappings
Same Client ID for all three. The kid in each token request picks the mapping, and with it the user and role.
NetSuite records the work under the mapped user
Whatever is done with a token is logged as done by the entity chosen when the mapping was created.
the user (entity) and role from the mapping
Not the administrator who uploaded the certificate.
One user per agent means you can always tell which agent did what.
